Your dreams stay on this phone. The microphone is used only while you are recording, and recordings never leave the phone.

The app goes online only to fetch the speech model for a language other than English, a download that carries nothing you have recorded, and, if you turn it on in Settings, to send the words of your dreams to your own Nextcloud. It connects only to the servers you set up, your sign-in details are kept on this phone encrypted, and nothing is sent to the app\'s maker.
If you keep dreams in Notes, Notes has the words. There are no ads, no analytics and no tracking. Exports go only where you choose to save them.

English is built in. Any other language needs a second listening model, about 60 MB, downloaded once from Hugging Face over the internet. That download is all the app ever fetches; nothing you record leaves the phone. Choosing English again deletes it.

Off. Your dreams stay on this phone.
Sending the words of your dreams

Dream Log can keep a copy of the words of your dreams in your own Nextcloud, so they survive losing this phone. It is off, and nothing leaves the phone, until you sign in here and turn on sending. Only the words go, as plain text files, never the recordings. They go over an encrypted https connection to the folder you choose.

Your Nextcloud password is never typed here: you sign in on Nextcloud\'s own page and it gives this phone an app password of its own, kept on the phone encrypted with a key held in its secure hardware. The files in Nextcloud are ordinary text, so anyone who can open that account can read them. With sending on, deleting a dream here deletes its copy there. Turning sending off leaves the copies already there. Nothing goes to the app\'s maker.
